'''Maria Teresa Rocha de Magalhães Melo''' (born 1966) is a Portuguese mathematician and [[operations research]]er who works as a professor in the business school of the {{ill|Saarland University of Applied Sciences|de|Hochschule für Technik und Wirtschaft des Saarlandes}} (htw saar), a [[Fachhochschule]] in [[Saarbrücken]], Germany.{{r|cv}} Her research interests include [[Optimal facility location|facility location]], [[supply chain management]], and in-hospital [[patient transport]].{{r|neue}}

==Education and career==
Melo was born in 1966 in [[Lisbon]],{{r|neue}} and studied applied mathematics at the [[University of Lisbon]], graduating in 1989 and earning a master's degree there in statistics and operations research in 1991. Next, she went to the Econometric Institute of [[Erasmus University Rotterdam]] for doctoral study, completing a PhD in operations research in 1996{{r|cv}} with a dissertation concerning the [[economic lot scheduling problem]].{{r|neue}}

She took postdoctoral research positions at the [[Forschungszentrum Jülich]] and {{ill|Fraunhofer Institute for Industrial Mathematics ITWM|lt=Fraunhofer Institute for Industrial Mathematics|de|Fraunhofer-Institut für Techno- und Wirtschaftsmathematik}} in 1997 and 1999 respectively, and became an invited lecturer at the [[Technical University of Kaiserslautern]] in 2000.{{r|cv}} She moved to htw saar as an associate professor in 2007,{{r|cv|neue}} and became a full professor in 2011. At htw saar, she is also founding co-director of the Institute for Supply Chain and Operations Management.{{r|cv}}
